summary: Rapid 5xx blips during tenant warmup caused by connection ramp and runtime GC
description: Issue summary: Customer (Acme Analytics) reports short, high-frequency 5xx spikes during morning traffic warmup window. Spikes are brief (30-90s) but recur across multiple tenants in the same tenant-group. Symptoms point to API gateway queueing + upstream runtime restarts coordinated with job of tenant prefetch/warmup and observed GC pauses on runtime nodes.
impact: Intermittent 500/502/503 errors observed for Acme Analytics' traffic during daily ramp; user-facing failures for chat sessions and short-generations. Estimated affected requests: ~12k over the 30-minute window. Business impact: degraded UX for enterprise customer during business hours; elevated support noise.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate tenant traffic ramp from 0 -> 200 concurrent connections over 2 minutes against redwood/gpt-3.8-medium.
2) Ensure tenant configured with aggressive prefetch/warmup (prefetch=true, warmup_concurrency=100).
3) Observe API gateway connection queue length and runtime pod GC logs during ramp.
4) Reproduce in prod-like staging with similar autoscaler thresholds to confirm behavior.
logs: 2026-03-12T08:11:23Z apigw[edge-23] WARN conn-queue=512 wait-ms=42 route=/v1/generate tenant=acme-123 status=queued
2026-03-12T08:11:55Z runtime[node-17] ERROR gc_pause_ms=1280 rss_mb=12460 model=gpt-3.8 pid=3121 message=major-gc-pause
2026-03-12T08:12:01Z apigw[edge-23] ERROR upstream=runtime node=node-17 status=502 upstream_err=connection-reset
2026-03-12T08:12:04Z runtime[node-17] INFO restart reason=oom-avoidance gc_trigger=true cmdline=--prefetch=on
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: sudden connection ramp during tenant warmup saturates API gateway connection queue and triggers head-of-line blocking; this amplifies request latencies which then cause runtime GC to kick in under high allocation pressure, producing long GC pauses and transient upstream 5xx responses.

Trace sampling shows majority of errors correlate with runtime node-17 and node-19 during 08:10-08:15 window. Node-level monitoring indicates increased minor/major GC activity and CPU contention aligning with error windows.
Autoscaler logs: rapid pod spin-up events coincide with warmup; readiness probes overlap with heavy prefetch work causing temporary unready states and additional request spillover into apigw queues.
API gateway metrics: conn_queue_length spikes to >400 for route /v1/generate; apigw threadpool shows syscall waits and 429 backpressure later in timeline.
Recreated in staging with scaled-down tenants reproduces 5xx blips when warmup_concurrency >= 80 and prefetch enabled. Disabling prefetch removes the blips in test.
Hypothesis tests: limiting warmup velocity (ramp rate) and capping prefetch work reduced GC pauses in staging; adding a short jitter to readiness probing prevented simultaneous unready->ready flaps.
comments: Maya Patel (Support): Logged by customer during morning ramp. Captured traces and alerted SRE. Initial mitigation requested: throttle tenant warmup or disable prefetch.
Liam O'Connor (SRE): Investigating runtime GC patterns and apigw queueing. Reproduced in staging. Recommend temporary ramp cap and GC tuning while we dig deeper.
Elena Ruiz (Eng - serving-runtime): Observed major GC on node-17 triggered by prefetch memory spike. We are preparing a small runtime patch to throttle prefetch worker concurrency during pod startup.
Customer (Acme): Confirmed disabling prefetch removes errors for now; requests an ETA for permanent fix and whether this will affect latency.
Liam O'Connor (SRE): Temporary mitigation applied to Acme tenant: warmup_rate set to 20 conn/min and prefetch disabled. Monitoring for 24 hours.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: applied tenant-level warmup_rate cap and disabled prefetch for Acme Analytics which removed immediate 5xx blips. Short-term plan: roll out runtime patch that limits prefetch worker concurrency during startup, adjust GC flags to reduce long major pauses, and add apigw adaptive queue backoff. Long-term: update warmup runbook to include staged ramp and modify autoscaler readiness timing. Target patch release: 2026-03-18.
next_steps: PR for runtime prefetch throttle: eng/serving-runtime#842 (in review)
Schedule runtime patch rollout to canary (small fleet) on 2026-03-16
Add an apigw circuit-breaker config for tenant warmup to avoid head-of-line amplification
Follow-up with customer on 2026-03-14 to confirm SLA status and share postmortem when complete
